title: English — CEFR path (A1 to C2)
description: A studio path from first words to mastery, one skill per module. Your teacher may skip modules you already know and add extra practice where you need it.
subject: English

modules.title: Greetings and introductions
modules.content: Say hello, give your name, where you are from, and ask the same of someone else.

modules.title: The verb to be
modules.content: I am, you are, she is. Positive, negative, and yes/no questions.

modules.title: Numbers, dates, and times
modules.content: Count to 100, say the date, and tell the time on the hour and half hour.

modules.title: Present simple — daily routines
modules.content: Describe a typical day with I get up, she works, they eat. Add the third-person -s.

modules.title: Everyday objects and places
modules.content: Core nouns for home, school, and town with a/an, this/that, and plurals.

modules.title: There is / there are
modules.content: Describe a room or a street. Use some and any with countable nouns.

modules.title: Reading short signs and notices
modules.content: Understand opening hours, prices, and simple instructions in public places.

modules.title: Writing a simple form and postcard
modules.content: Fill in personal details and write three or four sentences about a holiday.

modules.title: Past simple — regular verbs
modules.content: Talk about last weekend with -ed verbs. Pronunciation of /t/, /d/, /ɪd/.

modules.title: Past simple — irregular verbs
modules.content: The 30 most common irregular verbs in story form: went, saw, had, made.

modules.title: Comparatives and superlatives
modules.content: Compare cities, foods, and people: bigger, more interesting, the best.

modules.title: Shopping and ordering food
modules.content: Ask for things politely with Can I have… and Could I…? Handle prices and sizes.

modules.title: Future plans — going to
modules.content: Talk about plans and intentions for next week and next year.

modules.title: Understanding short messages
modules.content: Read texts, emails, and notes from friends and pick out the key information.

modules.title: Giving directions
modules.content: Go straight, turn left, it's opposite the bank. Ask for and follow directions.

modules.title: Writing a short personal email
modules.content: Invite, thank, or apologise in a short email with a clear opening and closing.

modules.title: Present perfect vs past simple
modules.content: Have you ever…? versus When did you…? Experience, unfinished time, and recent news.

modules.title: Narrative tenses
modules.content: Tell a story with past simple, past continuous, and past perfect in the right order.

modules.title: First and second conditionals
modules.content: Real and imagined situations: If it rains, we'll… / If I won, I would…

modules.title: Giving opinions and agreeing
modules.content: I think, in my view, I see your point but… Keep a simple discussion going.

modules.title: Reading for gist and detail
modules.content: Skim an article for the main idea, then scan for specific facts and numbers.

modules.title: Linking words for writing
modules.content: However, although, because of, as a result. Build connected paragraphs.

modules.title: Modal verbs of advice and obligation
modules.content: Should, must, have to, don't have to — and the difference in tone.

modules.title: Writing an informal letter or review
modules.content: Describe an experience and recommend it, with a clear structure and opinion.

modules.title: Passive voice in context
modules.content: Use the passive for processes, news, and formal writing. When to name the agent.

modules.title: Third and mixed conditionals
modules.content: Regrets and alternate pasts: If I had known… / If I'd studied, I'd be…

modules.title: Reported speech
modules.content: Report statements, questions, and requests with the right tense and word order.

modules.title: Discussing abstract topics
modules.content: Talk about work, technology, and society. Justify a view with examples.

modules.title: Reading opinion articles
modules.content: Identify the writer's stance, supporting arguments, and tone in a longer text.

modules.title: Essay structure — for and against
modules.content: Introduction, balanced body paragraphs, and a clear conclusion with your view.

modules.title: Collocations and phrasal verbs
modules.content: Make a decision, take part, put up with. Sound natural, not translated.

modules.title: Formal emails and complaints
modules.content: Register, polite directness, and requesting action in a professional email.

modules.title: Advanced verb patterns
modules.content: Gerund vs infinitive with change of meaning: stop to do / stop doing, remember, regret.

modules.title: Inversion and emphasis
modules.content: Not only… but also, Rarely have I…, What I need is… for emphasis in speech and writing.

modules.title: Hedging and softening
modules.content: It would seem that, arguably, to some extent. Express caution and nuance.

modules.title: Presenting and leading discussion
modules.content: Structure a short talk, signpost ideas, and manage questions confidently.

modules.title: Reading implied meaning
modules.content: Infer attitude, irony, and assumptions in literary and journalistic texts.

modules.title: Report and proposal writing
modules.content: Headings, objective tone, findings, and recommendations for a workplace audience.

modules.title: Idiomatic and fixed expressions
modules.content: Common idioms and fixed phrases, and when they are too informal to use.

modules.title: Cohesion across long texts
modules.content: Reference words, substitution, and ellipsis to keep long writing tight.

modules.title: Stylistic range and register shifts
modules.content: Move between academic, casual, and persuasive styles on the same topic.

modules.title: Subtle grammar distinctions
modules.content: Subjunctive, advanced modals of deduction, and nuanced article use.

modules.title: Debate and persuasion
modules.content: Build, rebut, and concede arguments fluently under time pressure.

modules.title: Critical reading of complex texts
modules.content: Evaluate argument quality, bias, and rhetorical technique in dense material.

modules.title: Summarising and synthesising sources
modules.content: Combine several sources into one accurate, concise summary in your own words.

modules.title: Precision vocabulary
modules.content: Choose the exact word: near-synonyms, connotation, and academic word families.

modules.title: Extended writing — the discursive essay
modules.content: A long, well-argued essay with sophisticated structure and a distinct voice.

modules.title: Spontaneous fluency and humour
modules.content: Handle unpredictable conversation, wordplay, and cultural references naturally.
